sections.html:
Georgetown is the Scott County seat and the sixth-largest city in Kentucky. The count was 37,086 in 2020, and the latest estimate is 40,883 (July 2025), a gain of 8.9% since April 2020. You can hire an agent, go it alone, or take a cash offer. Any of the three runs through county offices: the sheriff bills the tax, and the clerk records your deed and handles delinquent bills.

Prices run higher than in much of the state. Owners put the middle home value at $265,400, median gross rent is $1,255, and 62.3% of households own. Median household income is $80,088 across 14,899 households, with 2.56 people in the average one. Families with children under 18 made up 38.3% of households in 2020, which helps explain why bedrooms, a yard and a sound roof matter at showings.

Georgetown sits in the Bluegrass, north of Lexington. Interstate 75 passes east of downtown with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, putting downtown Lexington 16 miles south and Cincinnati 69 miles north. U.S. 25 runs through the center, U.S. 62 forms a bypass along the south and east, and U.S. 460 leads 18 miles west to Frankfort.

Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky opened in 1988 and anchors local hiring. The population went from 18,080 in 2000 to 29,098 in 2010. Workers at the plant and Lexington commuters tend to look near the interstate exits.

Summers are humid and about 45 inches of precipitation falls in a year. Before a showing, look over gutters, roof drainage and basement moisture, because a buyer's inspector will.

sections.h2: How Scott County collects property tax
sections.html:
Tax for 28 districts is collected by the Scott County Sheriff, who normally mails bills on November 1. Values come from somewhere else. For assessment questions, visit the Scott County PVA on the courthouse's second floor at 101 East Main Street, or phone (502) 863-7885.

Accepted payment types are cash, cashier's check, money order and card. A card adds a 2.75% vendor fee. Read the bill itself for due dates, ways to avoid penalties, and the steps when a mortgage servicer pays on your behalf.

Behind on taxes? The clerk's schedule shows how quickly costs stack up.

Delinquent tax timeline in Scott County
WhenWhat happens
April 15Delinquent certificates move to the County Clerk's office
May and JuneThe County Attorney mails two notices, and the first offers a payment agreement to eligible owners
June 30Last day to enter a payment agreement
July 1Advertising costs are added to bills still unpaid, which are published in the newspaper
Late summerPayment is due by a cutoff before the annual delinquent tax sale

By the time a bill transfers, it already carries a 10% penalty plus the sheriff's add-on fee, and interest builds at 1% per month. Request the clerk's payoff figure before you set a closing date. It is subtracted from your proceeds, so get it in hand early.

Kentucky charges the seller a deed tax of $0.50 for each $500 of value, rounding up to a whole block. The money goes to the Scott County Clerk when the deed is filed, in the courthouse building on East Main Street (number 101). Weekday office hours run 8:30 to 4:30, and the phone is (502) 863-7875.

Homestead exemption

Homeowners over 65 or totally disabled may qualify for the state homestead exemption, worth $49,100 of assessed value in the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Apply through the Scott County PVA. The benefit follows the owner, so your buyer files a fresh application.

One office issues building permits for both the city and Scott County: the City of Georgetown Building Inspection Department, 125 West Clinton Street. Zoning, plats and floodplain maps come from the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, whose website has a zoning map and a plat finder. Its phone is (502) 867-3701.

Finished a basement or built an addition? Ask the building department if those permits were closed out. Title review runs smoother when paperwork and house agree. If guests ever stayed by the night, ask the planning office whether a registration applies.

After you say yes to an offer, a closing agent or attorney orders a title search. It surfaces the mortgage, any unpaid tax certificate and any recorded lien, and each is paid or released out of your proceeds. Ask the sheriff and the clerk for written payoff letters several days early, so the settlement statement reflects what is actually owed.

At the table you sign the deed, pay the transfer tax to the clerk, and the deed is recorded in Scott County. Property tax for the months you owned the house is usually prorated on the statement. A cash buyer can often close on a date you pick because no appraisal or loan underwriting stands in the way. A financed buyer needs the lender's schedule, and a low appraisal can reopen price talks.

Moving out first? Keep utilities on until the deed is recorded, hand over keys and garage openers at closing, and keep copies of what you signed.

A cash purchase drops several steps that slow a Georgetown listing. No buyer's lender means no loan approval and no appraisal gap. Repairs stay with the buyer, so you are not haggling over a punch list after the inspection. Your closing date can be set around a move, an estate timeline or a tax deadline such as the June 30 payment-agreement cutoff.

The trade-off is price, since a cash buyer prices in the work and the risk. Ask for the offer in writing, with the deed tax, tax proration and any lien payoff spelled out, and compare it with the net from an agent sale after commission and repair credits.

Pull these together before comparing offers:

  • This year's and last year's tax bills from the sheriff, plus any delinquent certificate from the clerk.
  • A mortgage payoff statement, and the release for any other recorded lien.
  • Permit records from the City of Georgetown for additions or major repairs.
  • Leases and tenant contacts for any rented unit.

A house in good order with time to market suits an agent. A private sale needs an attorney for the contract and deed. Deferred repairs, tenants, delinquent taxes or an estate point toward a cash offer, which skips showings, appraisal and lender approval. Compare bids by what lands in your pocket after payoff, deed tax, prorated property tax and repair credits.

faqs.q: How much deed tax applies to a Georgetown sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $0.50 for every $500 of value, rounded up, at the Scott County Clerk's counter when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When does Scott County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff normally mails them on November 1. The bill lists the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Georgetown property taxes?
faqs.a: Around April 15 they move to the Scott County Clerk. The County Attorney mails notices in May and June, advertising costs attach on July 1, and a bill still open can go to the annual delinquent tax sale.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions on a Georgetown assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Scott County Property Valuation Administrator at (502) 863-7885. The sheriff collects the bill but does not set the value.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Georgetown?
faqs.a: The City of Georgetown's Building Inspection Department, 125 West Clinton Street, issues permits for both Georgetown and Scott County. Zoning and plat questions go to the Georgetown-Scott County Planning Commission, (502) 867-3701.
